title: Populous
shortDescription: Peter Molyneux and Bullfrog's revolutionary strategy title that single-handedly invented the 'God Game' genre.
historicalSignificance: Created an entirely new video game genre, allowing players to manipulate terrain as a deity to guide their followers against a rival god, selling over 4 million copies and defining early computer strategy design.

editorialContent.overview: Developed on the Amiga by Peter Molyneux and Glenn Corpes, Populous casts the player as a divine deity whose power is directly tied to the population size and civilization level of their mortal followers.
editorialContent.gameplay: Players raise and lower isometric terrain tiles to create flat plains where followers can build settlements. As faith grows, players unleash biblical divine interventions: earthquakes, swamps, volcanoes, and Armageddon.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Pioneered isometric dynamic land deformation in real time, accompanied by groundbreaking multi-computer modem-to-modem head-to-head multiplayer.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Earned universal acclaim, selling millions of copies and launching Peter Molyneux's storied design career, establishing Bullfrog as an industry powerhouse.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved across Amiga, Genesis, and SNES cartridges, as well as digital archival PC distribution.

awards: Origins Award for Best Military or Strategy Computer Game 1989
Inducted into CGW Hall of Fame
